synthesis: The paper gives a chain of representation changes for RH-sensitive zero information. For the repeated rational kernel, integration by parts turns a weighted arg zeta integral into an integral of Re(zeta'/zeta), while differentiating a parameterized log|zeta| identity reaches the same log-derivative interface and differentiates its off-line-zero corrections. Independently, the counting function turns a weighted sum over zero ordinates into an arg-zeta integral by Stieltjes integration, and the antiderivative S1 together with Littlewood's theorem turns that phase integral into a half-plane log-modulus integral; this is why the Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor formulations are rewritings rather than independent evidence. Multiplying zeta(z) by z-1 supplies a related pole-regularized modulus representation whose contour residues retain explicit, one-signed sensitivity to off-line zeros.
source_support: Unit openalex_w2005232657_v2_u04 derives the repeated-kernel arg-zeta/log-derivative relation by integration by parts and obtains the same interface by differentiating a weighted log-modulus identity, including differentiated zero corrections off RH. Unit openalex_w2005232657_v2_u06 writes N(x) as explicit terms plus arg zeta, identifies integration against dN with a weighted ordinate sum, and recovers Volchkov's arg-zeta criterion. Unit openalex_w2005232657_v2_u07 then integrates through S1 and applies Littlewood's horizontal log-modulus identity, explicitly concluding that the Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor criteria are the same criterion in different forms. Unit openalex_w2005232657_v2_u05 regularizes the pole with zeta(z)(z-1), relates critical-line and real-axis modulus integrals by a semi-indented contour, and shows that off-line zeros contribute same-sign residue terms.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compose the bridge objects across sections: dN converts a discrete zero statistic to boundary phase; integration by parts exposes Re(zeta'/zeta) from that phase; parameter differentiation exposes the same interface from a modulus family; and S1 plus Littlewood converts boundary phase to half-plane modulus. Pole cancellation changes the analytic object before contour deformation but leaves off-line-zero sensitivity visible in residues. This composition explains when different observables encode the same RH-sensitive divisor information and also locates where a representation change can fail.
limits: The source does not establish that every displayed correction has the identical formula after each transformation; differentiation, contour residues, and ordinate sums encode off-line zeros in representation-specific forms. The clean differentiated modulus baseline in unit u04 is introduced under RH, with the general case requiring added differentiated zero terms. Convergence, boundary decay, logarithm branches, principal-value interpretation, and Stieltjes/integration-by-parts hypotheses remain proof obligations. The indirect modulus route does not extend tractably to the two-scale kernel because the needed logarithmically weighted modulus integral is unavailable. Exact kernels, constants, contour weights, and normalizations in the OCR are scan-sensitive. Equivalence of criteria is not independent corroboration and finite numerical agreement cannot exclude all off-line zeros.
quality_reason: Accepted because distinct units jointly establish a concrete transformation network that no single parent contains: u06 supplies the zero-measure-to-phase bridge, u04 supplies the phase/modulus-to-log-derivative bridge and its differentiated corrections, and u07 supplies the phase-to-half-plane-modulus bridge and the explicit criterion equivalence; u05 adds a separate pole-regularized contour representation with residue sensitivity. The synthesis is therefore more than a shared theme, while its wording avoids claiming literal equality of all correction formulas or treating equivalent formulations as independent evidence.
